cluster: FILL: short name for this machine, e.g. delta
notes: Engine registry template — fill in the entries this cluster actually provides and delete the rest. You may not need this file at all: the built-in qe and lammps engines are configured in slab.toml under [engines.qe] and [engines.lammps]; the registry is for codes slab has no built-in for (VASP) and for pinning curated site setups under stable aliases. Rules: engine names must be lowercase and unpadded, and may not reuse a built-in name (emt, lammps, lj, qe, rootstock) — use a distinct alias like qe-delta. A retired built-in name (mace) is legal and is the migration path for scripts still using it. env may only hold variables the calculator reads at run time (VASP_PP_PATH, ASE_VASP_COMMAND); ASE_CONFIG_PATH is refused because ASE parses that file once at import, before any entry runs — declare command/pseudo_dir in options instead. Wire the filled file in via $SLAB_ENGINES, [paths] engines in slab.toml, or ~/.config/slab/engines.json. Entries execute as the calling user: trusting this file is trusting whoever edits it.

env.ASE_VASP_COMMAND: FILL: how to invoke VASP here, e.g. srun vasp_std

vasp.version: FILL: the installed version, e.g. 6.4.3 — recorded as provenance and folded into cache keys, so bump it when the module changes
vasp.description: VASP as installed on this cluster (licensed; slab has no built-in for it)

options.command: FILL: how to invoke pw.x here, e.g. srun pw.x — or env OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 pw.x to give just this engine its own environment variables

qe-mycluster.description: Optional pinned site alias for Quantum ESPRESSO, with all the built-in engine's guards. Only needed to curate a setup under a stable name — plain engine="qe" with [engines.qe] in slab.toml already covers the normal case. Rename to qe-<your cluster>.
